title: Route tiering and error-budget arbitrator spec for multi-region LLM endpoints
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem statement:
Redwood needs a deterministic, auditable mechanism to allocate and reclaim error budget across routes and model variants when capacity constraints occur (regional outages, burst loads). Current SLO decomposition exists but lacks an automated arbitration layer to decide: when to throttle, when to trigger circuit breakers, and when to gracefully degrade to lower-cost/latency model variants across regions. This ticket defines the "Error Budget Arbitrator" design, route-tiering taxonomy, SLI flavors, and operational runbook for staged load-shedding and multi-region failover.

Goals (what success looks like):
- Formalize per-route SLI definitions (latency P50/P95/P99, availability, request-quality for prompt sets) that map to route tiers.
- Define a route-tiering model (Platinum/Gold/Silver/BestEffort) with clear service guarantees and preemptive reclaim rules.
- Design the Error Budget Arbitrator (EBA): deterministic algorithm that holds short-term escrowed budgets, computes borrow/loan between routes, and enforces circuit-breaker thresholds.
- Specify multi-region failover decision criteria (health signals, capacity signal, regional burn-rate) and cross-region routing priorities.
- Produce a staged load-shedding policy with prioritized eviction list, model-variant substitution hierarchy, and observable decision points.
- Provide acceptance tests, dashboards, and a short runbook for on-call and SRE.

Proposed design (high-level):
1) Route tiering and SLI flavors:
   - Tier definitions:
     * Platinum: 99.9% availability, P95 latency target 150ms, request-quality SLI >= 99% on golden prompt set.
     * Gold: 99.5% availability, P95 latency target 300ms, request-quality SLI >= 97%.
     * Silver: 99% availability, P95 latency target 600ms, request-quality SLI >= 94%.
     * BestEffort: no availability SLA, latency best-effort.
   - SLI flavors: latency_quantiles, availability_5xx_free_rate, promptset_quality_score, tail_length (P99). Each route declares the flavor used in its service contract.

2) Error Budget Arbitrator (EBA):
   - Inputs: per-route SLI burn-rate (1h, 24h), current concurrency/queue length, regional capacity headroom, model-variant cost multiplier, and recent model-quality regression signals.
   - Operation: EBA maintains a short-lived escrow (configurable window, default 1h) per route. When burn-rate > threshold, EBA considers: temporary traffic shaping (rate-limit), downgrade to a compatible lower-quality variant, or preempt BestEffort/Lower-tier routes.
   - Arbitration policy: deterministic priority score = alpha * tier_priority + beta * (1 - burn_rate_norm) + gamma * customer_impact_score + delta * age_of_request. Tunable weights stored per-customer or per-tenant.
   - Reclamation: when a higher-tier route borrows from lower tiers, EBA creates a time-bound loan entry with automatic reclamation and a cooldown to avoid thrashing.

3) Circuit breakers & thresholds:
   - Soft circuit: triggered on P95 latency breach or queue depth > 90th percentile of baseline for 1 minute -> begin staged shedding.
   - Hard circuit: triggered on 5xx spike or sustained burn-rate > 3x baseline for 5 minutes -> force region-level reroute and aggressive shedding of BestEffort and Silver.
   - Breaker actions: traffic shaping, model variant substitution, regional failover, quota enforcement. All actions emit audit events.

4) Multi-region failover rules:
   - Health signals used: regional error_rate, tail_latency_ratio, model_variant_queue_depth, and regional_burn_rate.
   - Failover gating: only if target region has sufficient capacity headroom and its SLI projection over next 10 minutes remains within safe thresholds.
   - Traffic steering: weighted gradual shift (10% steps every 30s) with canary checks on golden prompt set until 100% or reversal if regressions detected.

5) Load-shedding and degradation hierarchy:
   - Eviction order (configurable): BestEffort -> Silver -> Gold (non-critical routes) -> Gold critical -> Platinum last.
   - Degradation actions per-step: reduce max_tokens, smaller model variant, disable non-essential response enrichment, turn off streaming (if applicable).

Telemetry & observability:
- New EBA dashboard showing escrow balances, active loans, per-route burn-rate, and arbitration decisions.
- Expose audit log for every arbitration decision with reason codes and impacted routes.
- Synthetic golden prompt set for each tier to validate model-quality during failover.
- Alerts: burn-rate runaway (>2x) per tier, long-lived loans (>1h), breaker flips > 3x / hour.

Testing & rollout plan:
- Unit tests for arbitration logic and deterministic scoring.
- Integration tests using chaos scenarios (regional capacity loss, delayed KV cache invalidation).
- Staged rollout: Canary in dev region (runtime-1.22 canary), internal beta customers opt-in, then gradual ramp to 25% production traffic with monitoring windows.

Runbook (short):
- If an arbitrator hard circuit triggers: check EBA dashboard -> identify top borrowers -> triage affected tenants -> if safe, trigger regional reroute to fallback region using console route override -> monitor golden promptset.
- If long-lived loans present: consider manual reclamation or scale-up.

Docs & links:
- Confluence spec (draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Route+Tiering+and+Error+Budget+Arbitrator
- Design notes and diagrams: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1X-eba-design
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3821

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Complexity vs predictability: EBA adds decision surface; we mitigate by deterministic scoring and thorough telemetry.
- Cross-tenant fairness: should loans be tenant-scoped or globally fungible? Default: tenant-scoped but allow global pool opt-in.
- Model-quality signals trust: need high-quality promptset and periodic re-validation to avoid incorrect downgrades.

Next steps (owners):
- Spec review with SRE and product (1 week) - Owner: Ravi Kapoor.
- Implement EBA prototype (2 sprints) - Owner: ENG-variant team.
- Dashboard and alerting (1 sprint) - Owner: Observability team.
- Runbook and on-call drills (1 sprint) - Owner: SRE.
acceptance_criteria: Per-route SLI flavors defined and registered in service contract registry
EBA prototype can simulate arbitration decisions deterministically against synthetic scenarios
Dashboard surfaces escrow balances and loan history with <30s freshness
Circuit breaker actions emit audit events and are reversible via console override
Staged canary shows no >1% regression on golden promptset for Platinum routes
